paras.en: They were often taken to the imperial capital of Cusco, where they participated in elaborate ceremonies before being sent to sacred sites throughout the empire. These processions could take months, traversing vast distances and difficult terrain before reaching their destinations.
paras.zh: 他们经常被带到帝国首都库斯科，在那里参加精心设计的仪式，然后被送往帝国各地的圣地。这些游行可能需要数月时间，穿越遥远的距离和崎岖的地形才能到达目的地。

paras.en: Some of the most sacred sites were high in the Andean mountains, where the children were buried with fine textiles, pottery, and precious figurines as offerings to the gods.
paras.zh: 一些最神圣的地点位于安第斯山脉的高处，孩子们埋葬在那里，里面埋葬着精美的纺织品、陶器和珍贵的雕像，作为献给神的祭品。

paras.en: It's long been known that these children were given drugs before they died, with traces of substances such as cocaine and alcohol found on multiple mummies.
paras.zh: 人们早就知道这些孩子在死前被注射了毒品，在多具木乃伊上发现了可卡因和酒精等微量物质。

paras.en: "Our main question was which psychoactive substances were given to children during the capacocha ritual and what purpose they served," Socha explained.
paras.zh: “我们的主要问题是在卡帕科查仪式期间向儿童提供了哪些精神活性物质以及它们的目的是什么，”索查解释道。

paras.en: "We wanted to understand whether they were used for medicinal reasons, to improve the children's wellbeing, or as part of religious practices involving altered states of consciousness."
paras.zh: “我们想了解它们是否被用于医疗目的、改善儿童的健康，或者作为涉及改变意识状态的宗教活动的一部分。”

paras.en: The answers, if there were any to be found, were most likely to be locked away in the bodies of the sacrificed children, mummified in the cold, low-oxygen environment in the Andean peaks.
paras.zh: 如果有任何答案的话，答案很可能被锁在被牺牲的儿童的尸体里，这些儿童在安第斯山峰寒冷、低氧的环境中被制成木乃伊。

paras.en: The researchers collected hair and nail samples from eight such mummies, dating to around 500 years ago.
paras.zh: 研究人员从八具这样的木乃伊身上收集了头发和指甲样本，其历史可以追溯到大约 500 年前。

paras.en: Keratin-rich tissues preserve chemical traces of substances consumed during life. As they grow, these traces become locked inside, allowing researchers to reconstruct aspects of a person's drug use in the weeks or months before death.
paras.zh: 富含角蛋白的组织保存了生命中消耗的物质的化学痕迹。随着它们的生长，这些痕迹被锁在里面，使研究人员能够重建一个人在死亡前几周或几个月内吸毒的各个方面。

paras.en: The researchers tested the samples for a range of psychoactive compounds, including stimulants, hallucinogens, and substances associated with medicinal plants.
paras.zh: 研究人员测试了样品中的一系列精神活性化合物，包括兴奋剂、致幻剂和与药用植物有关的物质。

paras.en: Coca use was widespread – which is perhaps not a huge surprise. The researchers detected cocaine and its metabolite benzoylecgonine in all six hair samples, consistent with the consumption of coca leaves – a practice deeply embedded in Andean culture.
paras.zh: 古柯的使用很广泛——这也许并不令人意外。研究人员在所有六个头发样本中检测到了可卡因及其代谢物苯甲酰爱康宁，这与食用古柯叶的情况一致——这种做法深深植根于安第斯文化中。

paras.en: Chewing coca leaves can help suppress hunger and fatigue, and may have helped the children endure the physical demands of their journeys through the mountains.
paras.zh: 咀嚼古柯叶可以帮助抑制饥饿和疲劳，并可能帮助孩子们忍受翻山越岭的身体需求。

paras.en: The researchers also detected cocaethylene in samples from some of the children. This compound is produced by the liver when cocaine and alcohol are present in the body at the same time – suggesting that these children had consumed both.
paras.zh: 研究人员还在一些儿童的样本中检测到了可卡乙烯。当可卡因和酒精同时存在于体内时，肝脏会产生这种化合物，这表明这些孩子同时摄入了这两种物质。

paras.en: The alcohol was likely consumed in the form of chicha, a fermented maize beer that played an important role in Inca religious ceremonies.
paras.zh: 这些酒精很可能以奇恰酒的形式消耗，这是一种发酵的玉米啤酒，在印加宗教仪式中发挥着重要作用。

paras.en: One especially tantalizing finding was harmine, detected in the nails of a 14-year-old girl known as the Ampato Maiden, or Juanita.
paras.zh: 一项特别诱人的发现是骆驼蓬碱，它在一名 14 岁女孩安帕托少女 (Ampato Maiden) 或胡安妮塔 (Juanita) 的指甲中检测到。

paras.en: Harmine is a psychoactive compound found in several plants, including Banisteriopsis caapi, a vine native to the Amazon rainforest and used in the preparation of ayahuasca. It inhibits an enzyme involved in breaking down certain neurotransmitters and may have mood-altering effects.
paras.zh: 骆驼蓬碱是一种在多种植物中发现的精神活性化合物，其中包括 Banisteriopsis caapi，一种原产于亚马逊雨林的藤本植物，用于制备死藤水。它抑制参与分解某些神经递质的酶，并可能具有改变情绪的作用。

paras.en: The researchers couldn't determine exactly which plant the girl had consumed, but its discovery in the Ampato Maiden follows its prior detection in two other child mummies from Mount Ampato and raises the interesting possibility that plants from the Amazon were transported to the Andes for ritual use.
paras.zh: 研究人员无法准确确定女孩食用的是哪种植物，但在安帕托少女中发现了这种植物，此前在安帕托山的另外两具儿童木乃伊中也发现了这种植物，并提出了一个有趣的可能性，即来自亚马逊的植物被运到安第斯山脉用于仪式用途。

paras.en: "What surprised me most was the diversity of the results," Socha said.
paras.zh: “最让我惊讶的是结果的多样性，”索查说。

paras.en: "Although coca consumption appears to have been common, we found considerable differences in the use of other substances. This suggests that the preparation of children was much more complex and varied than we previously thought."
paras.zh: “虽然古柯消费似乎很常见，但我们发现其他物质的使用存在相当大的差异。这表明儿童的准备工作比我们之前想象的要复杂和多样得多。”

paras.en: The researchers had also looked for evidence of substances that could induce hallucinations or altered states of consciousness, which might have played a role in preparing the children for their sacred duties.
paras.zh: 研究人员还寻找了可能引起幻觉或改变意识状态的物质的证据，这可能在孩子们为履行神圣职责做好准备方面发挥了作用。

paras.en: But here, the results told a rather different story.
paras.zh: 但在这里，结果却讲述了一个截然不同的故事。

paras.en: "The most important evidence is what we did not find," Socha said.
paras.zh: “最重要的证据是我们没有找到的，”索查说。

paras.en: "Despite testing for several hallucinogenic substances, including mescaline, DMT, and bufotenine, we found no traces of them in the analyzed samples."
paras.zh: “尽管对包括麦司卡林、DMT 和蟾蜍宁在内的几种致幻物质进行了测试，但我们在分析的样品中没有发现它们的痕迹。”

paras.en: Although Socha and her colleagues could not rule out a one-time use during the final stages of capacocha, which may have left no traces in hair and nails, the lack of hallucinogens suggests that the children may have been given drugs primarily to ease the physical and emotional hardships of their final journeys through the Andes, rather than to induce hallucinations.
paras.zh: 尽管索查和她的同事不能排除在卡帕科查的最后阶段一次性使用的可能性，这可能不会在头发和指甲上留下任何痕迹，但缺乏致幻剂表明，孩子们服用药物可能主要是为了缓解他们在穿越安第斯山脉的最后旅程中身体和情感上的困难，而不是诱发幻觉。

paras.en: One of the mummies offers a particularly poignant window into what those final months were like for some.
paras.zh: 其中一具木乃伊提供了一个特别令人心酸的窗口，让我们了解一些人最后几个月的生活。

paras.en: The hair of the mummy of an eight-year-old girl found on Mount Chuscha in Argentina preserved about six months of chemical history. By examining different parts of the hair, the researchers could trace the changes that may have occurred in that time.
paras.zh: 在阿根廷楚沙山发现的一名八岁女孩木乃伊的头发保存了大约六个月的化学历史。通过检查头发的不同部分，研究人员可以追踪当时可能发生的变化。

paras.en: Her coca intake seems to have fluctuated over those months, then dropped in the final month before she died – when she may also have begun ingesting alcohol
paras.zh: 她的古柯摄入量在这几个月里似乎有所波动，然后在她去世前的最后一个月下降——当时她可能也开始摄入酒精

paras.en: Socha cautions that this apparent change could also reflect differences in how the compounds became incorporated into the girl's hair, rather than a change in what she consumed – but there was no mistaking the evidence that she had consumed both.
paras.zh: 索查警告说，这种明显的变化也可能反映了这些化合物融入女孩头发的方式的差异，而不是她所吃东西的变化——但毫无疑问，有证据表明她同时吃过这两种化合物。

paras.en: The differences between the children may also be a clue about diversity within the Inca Empire.
paras.zh: 孩子们之间的差异也可能是印加帝国内部多样性的线索。

paras.en: "The Inca Empire included many different communities, religious traditions, and local deities. Although capacocha was an imperial ceremony, our results suggest that its practice was not identical everywhere," Socha said.
paras.zh: “印加帝国包括许多不同的社区、宗教传统和地方神灵。尽管卡帕科查是一种皇家仪式，但我们的研究结果表明，各地的做法并不相同，”索查说。

paras.en: The team hopes to investigate the substances used in these ceremonies in greater detail, for more insights into the children's origins, their lives before being selected for capacocha, and the preparations they underwent.
paras.zh: 研究小组希望更详细地调查这些仪式中使用的物质，以便更多地了解孩子们的起源、他们在被选中参加卡帕科查之前的生活以及他们所经历的准备工作。

paras.en: Meanwhile, Socha and her colleagues are also surveying sacred mountain sites in the Andes using technologies including drones, LiDAR, and ground-penetrating radar, hoping to build a more complete picture of the Inca's ritual landscape.
paras.zh: 与此同时，索查和她的同事还在利用无人机、激光雷达和探地雷达等技术对安第斯山脉的圣山遗址进行勘察，希望能够更全面地了解印加的仪式景观。

paras.en: "Mountain deities had their own characteristics and were believed to influence different aspects of people's lives, particularly water, climate, and agricultural fertility," Socha explained.
paras.zh: “山神有自己的特点，人们相信它们会影响人们生活的不同方面，特别是水、气候和农业肥力，”索查解释道。

paras.en: "It is possible that the differences we observe reflect the specific requirements of these deities and local religious traditions.
paras.zh: “我们观察到的差异可能反映了这些神灵和当地宗教传统的具体要求。

paras.en: "This reminds us that the Inca Empire was not a culturally uniform society. Imperial religious practices could incorporate considerable regional diversity."
paras.zh: “这提醒我们，印加帝国并不是一个文化统一的社会。帝国的宗教习俗可以包含相当大的地区多样性。”

paras.en: The research has been published in Antiquity.
paras.zh: 该研究已发表在《古代》杂志上。

articles.title: Just 3 Lines of Math Rule Out Time Travel in Many Possible Universes, Physicist Says
articles.author: Ivan Farkas

paras.en: Time travel is a dream shared by pretty much all of us.
paras.zh: 时间旅行是我们几乎所有人共同的梦想。

paras.en: But the dearth of visitors from the future – and the dismal turnout at the famed time traveler party – is alarming for hopefuls.
paras.zh: 但来自未来的游客的匮乏，以及著名的时间旅行者聚会的出席人数惨淡，令满怀希望的人感到震惊。

paras.en: Still, hypothetical time travel ideas abound, including traversable wormholes propped open by undiscovered exotic states of matter, and a rocket ship skirting billions of light-years around a spinning Universe to end up back in its past.
paras.zh: 尽管如此，假想的时间旅行想法仍然比比皆是，包括由未被发现的奇异物质态支撑的可穿越虫洞，以及一艘围绕旋转宇宙数十亿光年的火箭飞船最终回到过去。

paras.en: But a new study presents a surprisingly simple numerical basis for ruling out closed time loops in a wide class of possible universes, based on a single mathematical proof.
paras.zh: 但一项新的研究提出了一个令人惊讶的简单数值基础，基于单一的数学证明，可以排除多种可能宇宙中的闭合时间循环。

paras.en: In yet-to-be peer-reviewed research, posted to the preprint repository arXiv, physicist Hongsheng Zhang from the University of Jinan in China repurposed a long-standing equation to offer a new numerical prohibition against time travel – further dashing our hopes of a history-bending romp as promised by Bill & Ted's Excellent Adventure.
paras.zh: 在预印本存储库 arXiv 上发布的尚未经过同行评审的研究中，中国济南大学的物理学家张洪生重新利用了一个长期存在的方程，为时间旅行提供了新的数值禁止——进一步破灭了我们对比尔和泰德的《卓越冒险》中所承诺的扭转历史的嬉戏的希望。

paras.en: The research used the "null eikonal equation," an old tool for exploring how light propagates, to surprising effect.
paras.zh: 该研究使用了“零 eikonal 方程”，这是一种探索光如何传播的古老工具，取得了令人惊讶的效果。

paras.en: "The first is how little the theorem needs. The proof runs to three lines and uses exactly one fact about directions: a light-like direction can never be perpendicular to a traveller's direction in time," Zhang told ScienceAlert.
paras.zh: “首先是这个定理需要的东西有多么少。证明只有三行，并且只使用了一个关于方向的事实：类似光的方向永远不可能垂直于旅行者的时间方向，”张告诉 ScienceAlert。

paras.en: "From that alone it follows that a certain function must grow along every possible journey, so no journey can return to its starting event."
paras.zh: “仅从这一点就可以看出，某种功能必须沿着每一个可能的旅程发展，因此没有旅程可以返回到它的起始事件。”

paras.en: So a light beam can never be at a 90-degree angle (orthogonal) to the path of any entity moving through time – like a particle or a time traveler with a notepad full of winning lottery numbers – which means a certain quantity always increases along their journey, so they can never loop back.
paras.zh: 因此，光束永远不会与任何在时间中移动的实体的路径成 90 度角（正交）——就像一个粒子或一个带有写满中奖彩票号码的记事本的时间旅行者——这意味着一定的数量总是在他们的旅程中增加，所以他们永远不会回环。

paras.en: In other words, in such universes only forward movement is possible. As if driving down an endless one-way street with no service roads, turnarounds, or even an extended shoulder where one could pull over to enact a sneaky (illegal) U-turn.
paras.zh: 换句话说，在这样的宇宙中，只有向前运动是可能的。就好像沿着一条无尽的单行道行驶，没有辅助道路、转弯，甚至没有延伸的路肩，人们可以靠边停车偷偷地（非法）掉头。

paras.en: And, really, this is the basis of time travel, which has much different definitions depending on whether one is talking science or science fiction:
paras.zh: 事实上，这就是时间旅行的基础，根据人们谈论的是科学还是科幻小说，它有很多不同的定义：

paras.en: "People expect a result about time travel to need heavy machinery, energy conditions, quantum effects, maybe a singularity. It needs none of that. The whole content is bookkeeping about directions," Zhang adds.
paras.zh: “人们期望关于时间旅行的结果需要重型机械、能源条件、量子效应，也许还有奇点。它不需要这些。整个内容都是关于方向的簿记，”张补充道。

paras.en: The equational model used in this work offers a fourth family of criteria to prohibit closed time loops, supplementing the following three families:
paras.zh: 这项工作中使用的方程模型提供了第四个系列的标准来禁止闭合时间循环，补充了以下三个系列：

paras.en: First, the time function criteria state that time loops are ruled out if a universal clock can be defined that always ticks forward along every possible path.
paras.zh: 首先，时间函数标准规定，如果可以定义一个始终沿着每个可能路径向前滴答的通用时钟，则排除时间循环。

paras.en: Second, the energy condition criteria mandate that energy and gravity work in non-negative ways, disallowing time travel because it would require negative energy or "exotic matter".
paras.zh: 其次，能量条件标准要求能量和重力以非负的方式起作用，不允许时间旅行，因为它需要负能量或“奇异物质”。

paras.en: Third, topological criteria deal with the shape and connectivity of spacetime, linking time loops to the structure of the boundary where a time-travel region would begin.
paras.zh: 第三，拓扑标准涉及时空的形状和连通性，将时间循环与时间旅行区域开始的边界结构联系起来。

paras.en: Fortunately, this work adds an extra tool to theorists' time-traveling toolkit, allowing a relatively easy algebraic way to rule out numerical time-travel scenarios without messy mathematics that account for the greater Universe and its chaos.
paras.zh: 幸运的是，这项工作为理论家的时间旅行工具箱添加了一个额外的工具，允许一种相对简单的代数方法来排除数值时间旅行场景，而无需使用混乱的数学来解释更大的宇宙及其混乱。

paras.en: Another unexpected revelation is that one needs to find a way to turn part of the Universe into a churro to create a closed, time-traveling loop.
paras.zh: 另一个意想不到的启示是，人们需要找到一种方法将宇宙的一部分变成油条，以创建一个封闭的时间旅行循环。

paras.en: "So the surprise is that a question about the causal structure of an entire universe collapses into one scalar equation, and that the culprit is not spin. It is twist."
paras.zh: “所以令人惊讶的是，关于整个宇宙因果结构的问题可以分解为一个标量方程，而罪魁祸首不是自旋。而是扭曲。”

paras.en: Indeed, this is one of two escape routes that would allow time loops to exist, because a "sufficient condition is useful only if we know how it can fail."
paras.zh: 事实上，这是允许时间循环存在的两条逃生路线之一，因为“只有当我们知道它如何失败时，充分条件才有用。”

paras.en: As hinted, both escapes basically rely on spacetime folding back on itself to create a loop. This could happen locally, such as around a massive spinning black hole that turns spacetime into a pretzel, or if the layout of the Universe somehow doubles back on itself topologically.
paras.zh: 正如所暗示的，两种逃逸基本上都依赖于时空自身折叠来创建一个循环。这可能发生在局部，例如在一个巨大的旋转黑洞周围，将时空变成椒盐卷饼，或者如果宇宙的布局以某种方式在拓扑上加倍回来。

paras.en: Overall, this work splits the Universe based on light, rather than by moments of spacetime, which sidesteps our understanding of time.
paras.zh: 总的来说，这项工作是根据光而不是时空时刻来分裂宇宙，这回避了我们对时间的理解。

paras.en: "It is accurate to say we slice spacetime by light rather than by space. But the slices are not the paths of light; they are surfaces that light itself can inhabit."
paras.zh: “准确地说，我们是用光而不是空间来切片时空。但切片不是光的路径；它们是光本身可以居住的表面。”

paras.en: "Why does this help? An ordinary slice of space requires you to choose a moment, a moment requires a clock, and a clock requires an observer. A slice of light requires none of these. It is fixed by the geometry alone," Zhang explains.
paras.zh: “为什么这有帮助？一块普通的空间需要你选择一个时刻，一个时刻需要一个时钟，而一个时钟需要一个观察者。一片光不需要这些。它仅由几何形状固定，”张解释道。

paras.en: Finally, this offers a thought-and-math experiment of the type that has been influential throughout scientific history, allowing us to explore the abstruse principles that define our existence and possibilities.
paras.zh: 最后，这提供了一种在整个科学史上具有影响力的思想和数学实验，使我们能够探索定义我们的存在和可能性的深奥原理。

paras.en: But the Universe, as always, has the final say, Zhang concludes:
paras.zh: 但宇宙一如既往，拥有最终决定权，张总结道：

paras.en: "What it does not do is tell us whether nature permits any of this. That remains open, and it is the question I would most like to see answered."
paras.zh: “它没有告诉我们大自然是否允许这样做。这个问题仍然悬而未决，也是我最希望看到答案的问题。”

paras.en: But we are a step closer: "If you want a time machine, you now know exactly what you must break."
paras.zh: 但我们更近了一步：“如果你想要一台时间机器，你现在就知道必须打破什么。”

paras.en: The research has not yet been peer-reviewed, but a preprint is available on arXiv.
paras.zh: 该研究尚未经过同行评审，但 arXiv 上提供了预印本。

articles.title: A Huge Earthquake in Japan 7,300 Years Ago Pushed The Limits of Human Resourcefulness
articles.author: David Nield

paras.en: The Kikai-Akahoya volcanic eruption is one of the most destructive in history:
paras.zh: Kikai-Akahoya 火山喷发是历史上最具破坏性的火山喷发之一：

paras.en: Around 5250 BCE, almost 7,300 years ago, off the southwestern coast of Japan, it spewed massive amounts of magma and volcanic material from beneath the seabed in a series of blasts.
paras.zh: 大约在公元前 5250 年，也就是近 7,300 年前，日本西南海岸附近发生了一系列爆炸，从海底喷出了大量岩浆和火山物质。

paras.en: For the Jomon foraging communities of Japan at that time, it must've been a cataclysmic event of incomprehensible proportions. Scoring 7 out of 8 on the volcanic explosivity index, it's the sort of event that happens once every 500–1,000 years.
paras.zh: 对于当时日本的绳纹觅食社区来说，这一定是一场难以理解的灾难性事件。火山爆发指数为 7 分（满分 8 分），这种事件每 500-1000 年就会发生一次。

paras.en: Since evidence for the eruption was first discovered in the 1970s, experts have debated what its impacts were.
paras.zh: 自从 20 世纪 70 年代首次发现火山爆发的证据以来，专家们一直在争论其影响是什么。

paras.en: Clearly, the damage done by the eruption would've been extensive – but it's not clear if and when surrounding societies were able to recover, and to what extent, in the years that followed.
paras.zh: 显然，火山喷发造成的损害将是巨大的，但尚不清楚周边社会是否能够、何时能够恢复，以及在接下来的几年里恢复到什么程度。

paras.en: In a new study published in Science Advances, an international team of researchers has taken a closer look at the consequences of the Kikai-Akahoya volcanic eruption, finding that in some areas at least, humans were more resourceful and adaptable than had previously been thought.
paras.zh: 在《科学进展》杂志上发表的一项新研究中，一个国际研究小组仔细研究了 Kikai-Akahoya 火山喷发的后果，发现至少在某些地区，人类比以前想象的更足智多谋、适应能力更强。

paras.en: "This eruption must have been devastating, exploding out of the seabed with little warning," says archaeologist Peter Jordan, from Lund University in Sweden.
paras.zh: 瑞典隆德大学的考古学家彼得乔丹说：“这次火山喷发一定是毁灭性的，在没有任何预警的情况下从海底爆炸出来。”

paras.en: "It battered the Japanese islands with powerful earthquakes and enormous tsunamis, and then blanketed the landscape with meters of volcanic ash."
paras.zh: “它以强烈的地震和巨大的海啸袭击了日本岛屿，然后用数米厚的火山灰覆盖了大地。”

paras.en: The researchers looked at 540 existing archaeological samples collected across Japan, dated from 8,000 to 6,500 years ago – several hundred years before and after the eruption.
paras.zh: 研究人员对日本各地收集的 540 个现有考古样本进行了研究，这些样本的年代可追溯到 8,000 至 6,500 年前，即火山喷发前后的数百年。

paras.en: By tracking how many radiocarbon-dated finds (such as charcoal or bones) came from before and after the eruption in each region, they were able to assess population activity.
paras.zh: 通过追踪每个地区火山爆发前后有多少放射性碳测年发现物（例如木炭或骨头），他们能够评估人口活动。

paras.en: Some parts of the impact zone became uninhabitable for a very long time, the researchers found.
paras.zh: 研究人员发现，撞击区的某些部分在很长一段时间内变得无法居住。

paras.en: In other areas, there was evidence of people moving to new places, learning new skills, and adapting to a new way of life.
paras.zh: 在其他地区，有证据表明人们搬到新的地方，学习新的技能，并适应新的生活方式。

paras.en: "The disaster caused major loss of life," says archaeologist Enrico Crema, from Cambridge University in the UK.
paras.zh: 英国剑桥大学的考古学家恩里科·克雷马说：“这场灾难造成了重大人员伤亡。”

paras.en: "However, survivors migrated, forged new social relations, innovated new kinds of economy, and appear to have found creative ways to exist and later thrive in the new post-disaster conditions."
paras.zh: “然而，幸存者迁移，建立了新的社会关系，创新了新型经济，似乎找到了创造性的生存方式，并在新的灾后条件下蓬勃发展。”

paras.en: The researchers found that traditional Jomon forager populations may already have been declining in southern Kyushu, closest to the eruption, even before it happened.
paras.zh: 研究人员发现，在距离火山喷发最近的九州南部，甚至在火山喷发之前，传统绳纹觅食者的数量可能就已经在下降。

paras.en: In contrast, the size and number of communities in the north of the island were on the rise before the eruption – and this trend continued afterward. This resilience may be evidence of affected groups moving away from the disaster area, the study suggests.
paras.zh: 相比之下，该岛北部社区的规模和数量在火山喷发前一直在增加，而且这种趋势在喷发后仍在继续。研究表明，这种恢复力可能是受影响群体离开灾区的证据。

paras.en: Marine life seems to have recovered the quickest, and the movement of Japan's prehistoric people followed. The researchers suggest inland survivors may have made their way to the coasts and adapted to a new way of living there.
paras.zh: 海洋生物似乎恢复得最快，日本史前人类的迁徙也紧随其后。研究人员认为，内陆幸存者可能已经前往海岸并适应了那里的新生活方式。

paras.en: "Even in the most impossible situations, survivors and communities have choices, however limited," says Jordan.
paras.zh: “即使在最不可能的情况下，幸存者和社区也有选择，无论选择多么有限，”乔丹说。

paras.en: "They need to act and make decisions; they need to adjust, collaborate, and find new connections and social networks."
paras.zh: “他们需要采取行动并做出决定；他们需要调整、协作并寻找新的联系和社交网络。”

paras.en: The researchers also found that some more distant areas of Japan, such as around Ise Bay, where population numbers had been increasing, saw this growth halt and even decline in certain areas.
paras.zh: 研究人员还发现，日本一些较远的地区，例如伊势湾周围，人口数量一直在增加，但某些地区的人口增长停止甚至下降。

paras.en: The team thinks this may be due to short-term cooling triggered by the eruption or an as-yet-unidentified effect of climate change.
paras.zh: 研究小组认为，这可能是由于火山喷发引发的短期降温或气候变化尚未确定的影响所致。

paras.en: Or it may possibly be down to a loss of food sources: Grazing in ash-covered landscapes may have worn down the teeth of deer and boar, shortening their lives.
paras.zh: 或者可能是由于食物来源的丧失：在灰烬覆盖的地区放牧可能磨损了鹿和野猪的牙齿，缩短了它们的寿命。

paras.en: The findings give us a better idea of how humankind can respond to natural disasters and dig deep to survive – something which is becoming ever more relevant in a world that's seeing major shifts in climate and weather.
paras.zh: 这些发现让我们更好地了解人类如何应对自然灾害并深入挖掘生存——这在气候和天气发生重大变化的世界中变得越来越重要。

paras.en: "This study helps in creating a deeper understanding of the contingent ways in which cultures and societies cope with sudden shocks and catastrophes," says Jordan.
paras.zh: 乔丹说：“这项研究有助于更深入地了解文化和社会应对突发冲击和灾难的偶然方式。”

paras.en: The research has been published in Science Advances.
paras.zh: 该研究已发表在《科学进展》上。

articles.title: Scientists just found a loophole that could let black holes split in two

paras.en: Scientists just found a loophole that could let black holes split in two
paras.zh: 科学家刚刚发现了一个可以让黑洞一分为二的漏洞

paras.en: - Scientists have discovered a possible loophole in the laws that normally prevent black holes from splitting apart, suggesting that extremely fast-spinning black holes might divide into two. The surprising finding raises the possibility of an entirely new black hole phenomenon that future telescopes could potentially detect.
paras.zh: - 科学家们发现了通常阻止黑洞分裂的法律中可能存在的漏洞，这表明旋转速度极快的黑洞可能会一分为二。这一令人惊讶的发现提出了未来望远镜可能探测到的全新黑洞现象的可能性。

paras.en: Black holes are known for merging when two of them collide, but could the reverse ever happen? Could a single black hole somehow divide into two smaller ones? A new theoretical study suggests that this extraordinary possibility may not be entirely ruled out by physics, although the conditions required would be extreme.
paras.zh: 众所周知，黑洞在两个碰撞时会合并，但相反的情况会发生吗？一个黑洞能否以某种方式分裂成两个较小的黑洞？一项新的理论研究表明，物理学可能无法完全排除这种非凡的可能性，尽管所需的条件非常极端。

paras.en: The research, published in Physical Review D under the title "When Black Holes Admit Pair-of-pants Topologies," examines the physical laws that keep black holes intact and whether certain circumstances could allow them to break apart.
paras.zh: 这项研究发表在《物理评论 D》上，标题为“当黑洞承认裤子拓扑时”，研究了保持黑洞完整的物理定律，以及某些情况是否会允许它们分裂。

paras.en: "In our study, we investigate which physical laws normally prevent a black hole from splitting into two. We also investigate if certain circumstances may allow a split to happen," says Francesco Sannino, co-author of the study and a professor of physics at University of Naples Federico II in Italy and Quantum Field Theory Center at University of Southern Denmark.
paras.zh: 该研究的合著者、意大利那不勒斯费德里科二世大学和南丹麦大学量子场论中心的物理学教授弗朗西斯科·桑尼诺（Francesco Sannino）表示：“在我们的研究中，我们研究了哪些物理定律通常会阻止黑洞分裂成两半。我们还研究了某些情况是否可能允许分裂发生。”

paras.en: The research team also included Giacomo Cacciapaglia, a researcher with the French National Centre for Scientific Research (CNRS) at the Laboratoire de Physique Théorique et Hautes Énergies, a joint CNRS and Sorbonne Université laboratory in Paris. Additional contributors were Manuel Del Piano and Vania Vellucci, both from the Quantum Field Theory Center at the University of Southern Denmark.
paras.zh: 该研究小组还包括法国国家科学研究中心（CNRS）物理理论和高级能源实验室（法国国家科学研究中心和巴黎索邦大学的联合实验室）的研究员贾科莫·卡恰帕利亚（Giacomo Cacciapaglia）。其他贡献者包括来自南丹麦大学量子场论中心的 Manuel Del Piano 和 Vania Vellucci。

paras.en: Why Black Holes Normally Cannot Split Apart
paras.zh: 为什么黑洞通常不能分裂

paras.en: One of the biggest obstacles to a black hole splitting comes from thermodynamics, the branch of physics that governs how energy behaves and how physical systems change.
paras.zh: 黑洞分裂的最大障碍之一来自热力学，它是控制能量行为和物理系统如何变化的物理学分支。

paras.en: A central concept is entropy, which describes how many different microscopic arrangements a system can have while appearing unchanged from the outside. Black holes have entropy, and this property places important limits on what can happen to them.
paras.zh: 一个核心概念是熵，它描述了一个系统在从外部看起来没有变化的情况下可以有多少种不同的微观排列。黑洞具有熵，这一特性对它们可能发生的事情施加了重要的限制。

paras.en: For a black hole that is not rotating, dividing into two smaller black holes would reduce the total entropy. Such a decrease makes the process thermodynamically unfavorable, helping explain why black holes do not ordinarily break apart.
paras.zh: 对于不旋转的黑洞，分成两个较小的黑洞会减少总熵。这种减少使得该过程在热力学上不利，这有助于解释为什么黑洞通常不会分裂。

paras.en: However, the researchers found that the situation could change dramatically when a black hole spins at an exceptionally high speed.
paras.zh: 然而，研究人员发现，当黑洞以极高的速度旋转时，情况可能会发生巨大变化。

paras.en: Extreme Rotation Could Allow Black Holes to Split
paras.zh: 极端旋转可能导致黑洞分裂

paras.en: The team's calculations suggest that rapid rotation may create a narrow opening in the physical rules that normally prevent black holes from dividing. In principle, a sufficiently fast spinning black hole could overcome the usual thermodynamic restriction.
paras.zh: 该团队的计算表明，快速旋转可能会在通常阻止黑洞分裂的物理规则中产生一个狭窄的开口。原则上，足够快旋转的黑洞可以克服通常的热力学限制。

paras.en: But there is another major obstacle. Even if a black hole could divide, the two resulting objects would need to move far enough apart to avoid immediately merging again.
paras.zh: 但还有另一个主要障碍。即使黑洞可以分裂，产生的两个物体也需要移动得足够远，以避免立即再次合并。

paras.en: "But the two resulting black holes must also be able to separate rather than immediately fall back together. When we include this requirement, the window largely closes again, except possibly for black holes rotating close to their maximum possible rate," says Francesco Sannino.
paras.zh: “但是由此产生的两个黑洞也必须能够分离，而不是立即回落到一起。当我们考虑到这一要求时，窗口基本上会再次关闭，除非黑洞旋转速度接近其最大可能速度，”弗朗西斯科·桑尼诺说。

paras.en: The study's unusual title refers to the shape that a black hole's boundary would trace through space and time if such a split occurred. This boundary, called the horizon, would begin as a single structure before separating into two distinct branches.
paras.zh: 这项研究的不同寻常的标题指的是如果发生这种分裂，黑洞的边界在空间和时间上所描绘出的形状。这个边界称为地平线，最初是一个单一的结构，然后分成两个不同的分支。

paras.en: Viewed across time, the resulting shape would resemble a pair of trousers, with one upper section dividing into two "legs." This is the idea behind the term "pair-of-pants topologies."
paras.zh: 从时间上看，最终的形状类似于一条裤子，上半部分分为两条“腿”。这就是术语“裤子拓扑”背后的想法。

paras.en: Extra Dimensions Offer Another Possibility
paras.zh: 额外的尺寸提供了另一种可能性

paras.en: The researchers also investigated more unusual scenarios involving theories in which space has additional dimensions beyond the three we experience in everyday life.
paras.zh: 研究人员还研究了更不寻常的场景，其中涉及的理论是，空间具有超出我们日常生活中所经历的三个维度的额外维度。

paras.en: Physicists have already identified objects resembling black holes in some of these theoretical models that can become unstable and start breaking apart. These possibilities suggest that the familiar rules governing black holes may not apply in the same way under more exotic conditions.
paras.zh: 物理学家已经在其中一些理论模型中发现了类似黑洞的物体，这些物体可能会变得不稳定并开始分裂。这些可能性表明，在更奇特的条件下，熟悉的黑洞规则可能不会以同样的方式适用。

paras.en: In certain cases, splitting could even become thermodynamically favorable, especially when one of the two resulting black holes is much smaller than the other.
paras.zh: 在某些情况下，分裂甚至可能在热力学上变得有利，特别是当产生的两个黑洞之一比另一个小得多时。

paras.en: However, a process being allowed or favored by thermodynamics does not necessarily mean it will happen. Researchers still need to determine whether such fragmentation can physically occur and what conditions would make it possible.
paras.zh: 然而，热力学允许或支持的过程并不一定意味着它会发生。研究人员仍然需要确定这种碎片是否会在物理上发生以及什么条件可以实现。

paras.en: Could Astronomers Detect a Black Hole Splitting?
paras.zh: 天文学家能探测到黑洞分裂吗？

paras.en: The scientists are now working to better understand how likely these events might be. The answer may depend on aspects of gravity that go beyond Einstein's theory, making the problem especially challenging.
paras.zh: 科学家们现在正在努力更好地了解这些事件发生的可能性。答案可能取决于超出爱因斯坦理论的引力方面，这使得这个问题特别具有挑战性。

paras.en: "We cannot yet give a single probability for a black hole to split. It depends on how gravity behaves beyond Einstein's theory, and we are working to quantify this. We expect small primordial black holes to be more prone to splitting than much larger astrophysical black holes. We may detect a split indirectly: gamma-ray telescopes such as Fermi-LAT can search for signals from tiny black-hole fragments that might form during mergers," says Francesco Sannino.
paras.zh: “我们还不能给出黑洞分裂的单一概率。这取决于引力在爱因斯坦理论之外的表现，我们正在努力量化这一点。我们预计小型原始黑洞比大得多的天体物理黑洞更容易分裂。我们可以间接检测到分裂：像费米-LAT这样的伽马射线望远镜可以从合并过程中可能形成的微小黑洞碎片中搜索信号，”弗朗西斯科·桑尼诺说。

paras.en: Although there is currently no confirmed observation of a black hole splitting, the possibility of detecting signals from tiny fragments offers a potential way to investigate the idea. Such evidence could provide valuable clues about the behavior of gravity under some of the most extreme conditions in the universe.
paras.zh: 尽管目前还没有确认黑洞分裂的观测结果，但检测微小碎片信号的可能性为研究这一想法提供了一种潜在的方法。这些证据可以为宇宙中一些最极端条件下的引力行为提供有价值的线索。

paras.en: Sannino is the director of the Quantum Field Theory Center (ℏQTC), which is affiliated with the Department of Mathematics and Computer Science (IMADA) at the University of Southern Denmark. He is also affiliated with the Danish Institute for Advanced Study and the Department of Physics "Ettore Pancini" at the University of Naples Federico II. In addition, he serves as a visiting professor at Durham University.
paras.zh: Sannino 是量子场论中心 (ℏQTC) 的主任，该中心隶属于南丹麦大学数学与计算机科学系 (IMADA)。他还隶属于丹麦高等研究院和那不勒斯费德里科二世大学物理系“Ettore Pancini”。此外，他还是杜伦大学的客座教授。

paras.en: Materials provided by University of Southern Denmark. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
paras.zh: 材料由南丹麦大学提供。注意：内容可能会根据样式和长度进行编辑。

paras.en: - Giacomo Cacciapaglia, Manuel Del Piano, Francesco Sannino, Vania Vellucci. When black holes admit pair-of-pants topologies. Physical Review D, 2026; 114 (8) DOI: 10.1103/cx69-t466
paras.zh: - 贾科莫·卡恰帕利亚、曼努埃尔·德尔·皮亚诺、弗朗西斯科·桑尼诺、瓦尼亚·韦鲁奇。当黑洞承认裤子拓扑时。物理评论D，2026； 114（8）DOI：10.1103/cx69-t466

articles.title: Large Hadron Collider reveals evidence of Big Bang matter in surprisingly small collisions

paras.en: Large Hadron Collider reveals evidence of Big Bang matter in surprisingly small collisions
paras.zh: 大型强子对撞机在令人惊讶的小碰撞中揭示了大爆炸物质的证据

paras.en: - Scientists at CERN's Large Hadron Collider have uncovered compelling new evidence that even relatively small atomic collisions can recreate the extraordinary state of matter that filled the universe moments after the Big Bang. Known as quark-gluon plasma, this exotic substance forms at temperatures more than 100,000 times hotter than the center of the Sun, causing ordinary particles to break apart into their fundamental building blocks.
paras.zh: -欧洲核子研究组织大型强子对撞机的科学家们发现了令人信服的新证据，表明即使相对较小的原子碰撞也可以重现大爆炸后充满宇宙的非凡物质状态。这种奇特的物质被称为夸克-胶子等离子体，其形成温度比太阳中心高10万倍以上，导致普通粒子分解成基本构件。

paras.en: The findings come one year after the first-ever oxygen collisions at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC). All four of the collider's major research collaborations, ALICE, ATLAS, CMS and LHCb, have now reported signs that this primordial form of matter can emerge when oxygen and neon nuclei collide.
paras.zh: 这一发现是在大型强子对撞机 (LHC) 首次发生氧气碰撞一年后得出的。对撞机的所有四个主要研究合作机构，ALICE、ATLAS、CMS 和 LHCb，现在都报告了有迹象表明，当氧核和氖核碰撞时，会出现这种原始形式的物质。

paras.en: The results challenge a long-standing assumption about the enormous forces needed to create such an extreme substance. They also offer scientists a new way to investigate the conditions that prevailed during the universe's earliest moments.
paras.zh: 这些结果挑战了长期以来关于创造这种极端物质需要巨大力量的假设。它们还为科学家提供了一种研究宇宙最初时刻普遍存在的条件的新方法。

paras.en: Recreating the Extreme Matter of the Early Universe
paras.zh: 重建早期宇宙的极端物质

paras.en: Quark–gluon plasma (QGP) is an unusual state of matter that appears under tremendous pressure and heat. At temperatures exceeding 100,000 times those at the Sun's center, particles such as protons and neutrons can no longer maintain their normal structure. Instead, they break apart into quarks and the gluons that ordinarily bind them together.
paras.zh: 夸克-胶子等离子体（QGP）是一种不寻常的物质状态，在巨大的压力和热量下出现。当温度超过太阳中心温度的 100,000 倍时，质子和中子等粒子将无法再维持其正常结构。相反，它们分裂成夸克和通常将它们结合在一起的胶子。

paras.en: Physicists believe that this was the state of matter throughout the universe during the first millionths of a second after the Big Bang. Nearly 14 billion years later, researchers can briefly recreate these extraordinary conditions by smashing atomic nuclei together at extremely high energies inside the LHC.
paras.zh: 物理学家认为，这是大爆炸后最初百万分之一秒内整个宇宙的物质状态。近 140 亿年后，研究人员可以通过在大型强子对撞机内以极高能量将原子核粉碎在一起来短暂地重现这些非凡的条件。

paras.en: For decades, scientists believed that generating this plasma required collisions involving very heavy atomic nuclei, particularly lead. Lead nuclei are more than 200 times heavier than the protons typically used in LHC experiments, making them capable of producing the intense conditions thought necessary for QGP to form.
paras.zh: 几十年来，科学家们认为，产生这种等离子体需要涉及非常重的原子核，特别是铅的碰撞。铅核比大型强子对撞机实验中通常使用的质子重 200 多倍，这使得它们能够产生 QGP 形成所需的强烈条件。

paras.en: However, recent discoveries have increasingly called that assumption into question.
paras.zh: 然而，最近的发现越来越多地对这一假设提出质疑。

paras.en: Earlier this year, the ALICE collaboration, which specializes in studying quark–gluon plasma, identified another indication of QGP formation in proton–proton and proton–lead collisions. The previous year, LHC researchers had also reported the first hints of this plasma emerging from oxygen–oxygen collisions.
paras.zh: 今年早些时候，专门研究夸克-胶子等离子体的 ALICE 合作组织发现了质子-质子和质子-铅碰撞中 QGP 形成的另一个迹象。去年，大型强子对撞机研究人员还报告了氧-氧碰撞中出现这种等离子体的第一个迹象。

paras.en: Now, more detailed investigations have revealed multiple signs that QGP can form in collisions involving both oxygen and neon nuclei, providing stronger evidence that the conditions required to create this primordial matter are not limited to heavy atomic collisions.
paras.zh: 现在，更详细的研究揭示了多种迹象，表明 QGP 可以在涉及氧核和氖核的碰撞中形成，这提供了更有力的证据，证明创造这种原始物质所需的条件不仅限于重原子碰撞。

paras.en: Scientists Detect Evidence of Energy Loss in Extreme Collisions
paras.zh: 科学家发现极端碰撞中能量损失的证据

paras.en: One of the clearest ways to identify quark–gluon plasma is to examine what happens when energetic quarks and gluons travel through it.
paras.zh: 识别夸克-胶子等离子体的最清晰方法之一是检查当高能夸克和胶子穿过它时会发生什么。

paras.en: As these particles move through the extremely hot and dense material, they lose some of their energy. Scientists call this process parton energy loss, and it provides an important clue that QGP has formed.
paras.zh: 当这些粒子穿过极热且致密的材料时，它们会损失一些能量。科学家将这一过程称为部分能量损失，它为QGP的形成提供了重要线索。

paras.en: The ATLAS collaboration clearly detected this effect by studying pairs of particle jets generated during oxygen–oxygen and neon–neon collisions. These jets are concentrated streams of particles produced when energetic quarks and gluons emerge from a collision.
paras.zh: ATLAS 合作通过研究氧-氧和氖-氖碰撞过程中产生的粒子射流对，清楚地发现了这种效应。这些喷流是高能夸克和胶子碰撞时产生的集中粒子流。

paras.en: Researchers observed differences in energy between the paired jets, indicating that some of the particles had lost energy while traveling through the surrounding material.
paras.zh: 研究人员观察到成对喷流之间的能量差异，这表明一些粒子在穿过周围材料时损失了能量。

paras.en: The effect was especially pronounced during more direct, head-on (central) collisions. Such impacts are expected to create a larger volume of plasma, giving particles more material to travel through and causing greater energy loss.
paras.zh: 在更直接的正面（中央）碰撞中，这种影响尤其明显。这种影响预计会产生更大体积的等离子体，使粒子有更多的物质可以穿过，并造成更大的能量损失。

paras.en: Preliminary ATLAS results provide additional support for this interpretation. By examining charged particles that recoil in the opposite direction from photons, researchers found a similar relationship between energy loss and how centrally the nuclei collided.
paras.zh: ATLAS 的初步结果为这一解释提供了额外的支持。通过检查与光子相反方向反冲的带电粒子，研究人员发现能量损失与原子核碰撞的中心程度之间存在类似的关系。

paras.en: Multiple CERN Experiments Confirm the Pattern
paras.zh: 多项 CERN 实验证实了这一模式

paras.en: The ALICE, CMS, and LHCb collaborations searched for the same underlying process using a different approach. Rather than focusing primarily on the energy of particle jets, they examined how the plasma appears to reduce the production of certain energetic particles.
paras.zh: ALICE、CMS 和 LHCb 合作使用不同的方法寻找相同的底层过程。他们没有主要关注粒子射流的能量，而是研究了等离子体如何减少某些高能粒子的产生。

paras.en: CMS found that charged-particle production was suppressed in both oxygen–oxygen and neon–neon collisions compared with proton–proton collisions. This reduction is consistent with particles losing energy inside quark–gluon plasma and provides further evidence that the exotic material can form in collisions involving lighter nuclei.
paras.zh: CMS 发现，与质子-质子碰撞相比，氧-氧碰撞和氖-氖碰撞中带电粒子的产生受到抑制。这种减少与夸克-胶子等离子体内的粒子失去能量是一致的，并提供了进一步的证据，表明奇异材料可以在涉及较轻原子核的碰撞中形成。

paras.en: LHCb reported another important clue in a separate study. The collaboration investigated particles containing a charm quark and a lighter quark, comparing how strongly their production was suppressed in oxygen and neon collisions.
paras.zh: LHCb 在另一项研究中报告了另一个重要线索。该合作研究了含有粲夸克和轻夸克的粒子，比较了它们的产生在氧和氖碰撞中受到抑制的程度。

paras.en: The suppression was more pronounced in the heavier neon collisions. That is precisely the kind of behavior scientists would expect if larger collisions produce greater volumes of plasma, causing particles to lose more energy as they pass through it.
paras.zh: 在较重的霓虹灯碰撞中，这种抑制更为明显。如果更大的碰撞产生更大体积的等离子体，导致粒子在穿过等离子体时损失更多能量，这正是科学家们所期望的行为。

paras.en: However, reduced particle production does not necessarily prove that energy loss is responsible. Other physical processes could potentially produce similar effects.
paras.zh: 然而，粒子产生的减少并不一定证明能量损失是造成这种情况的原因。其他物理过程也可能产生类似的效果。

paras.en: To investigate this possibility, ALICE compared the production of neutral pions, another type of subatomic particle, in oxygen–oxygen and proton–oxygen collisions.
paras.zh: 为了研究这种可能性，ALICE 比较了氧-氧和质子-氧碰撞中中性介子（另一种亚原子粒子）的产生。

paras.en: The comparison provided unambiguous evidence of parton energy loss in oxygen–oxygen collisions, strengthening the case that even relatively small nuclear collisions can generate conditions associated with quark–gluon plasma.
paras.zh: 这一比较提供了氧-氧碰撞中部分子能量损失的明确证据，强化了即使相对较小的核碰撞也能产生与夸克-胶子等离子体相关的条件的论点。

paras.en: More Clues Emerge From Exotic Subatomic Particles
paras.zh: 更多线索来自奇异的亚原子粒子

paras.en: Researchers also looked for another distinctive signature of QGP involving particles made from a heavy quark and its corresponding antiquark.
paras.zh: 研究人员还寻找 QGP 的另一个独特特征，涉及由重夸克及其相应的反夸克组成的粒子。

paras.en: These pairs can briefly bind together following high-energy collisions. Some are more tightly bound than others, making them differently susceptible to disruption by the surrounding plasma.
paras.zh: 这些对可以在高能碰撞后短暂地结合在一起。有些比其他结合更紧密，使得它们更容易受到周围等离子体的破坏。

paras.en: By examining which bound states are suppressed and by how much, physicists can gather additional evidence about whether QGP is present.
paras.zh: 通过检查哪些束缚态被抑制以及抑制程度，物理学家可以收集关于 QGP 是否存在的更多证据。

paras.en: The CMS collaboration found evidence of this varying suppression in particles called upsilon mesons, which consist of a bottom quark paired with its antiquark. The researchers identified the effect by comparing oxygen–oxygen and neon–neon collisions.
paras.zh: CMS 合作发现了被称为 upsilon 介子的粒子存在这种不同抑制的证据，该粒子由与其反夸克配对的底夸克组成。研究人员通过比较氧-氧和氖-氖碰撞来确定这种效应。

paras.en: LHCb also reported preliminary evidence of similar behavior, this time using data from proton–oxygen and oxygen–oxygen collisions.
paras.zh: LHCb 也报告了类似行为的初步证据，这次使用的是质子-氧和氧-氧碰撞的数据。

paras.en: Together, these observations add another piece to the growing body of evidence that primordial plasma can emerge in nuclear collisions much smaller than those traditionally used to study it.
paras.zh: 总之，这些观察结果为越来越多的证据增添了另一条证据，表明原始等离子体可以在比传统用于研究它的核碰撞小得多的核碰撞中出现。

paras.en: Unexpected Particle Patterns Offer Another Hint
paras.zh: 意想不到的粒子模式提供了另一个提示

paras.en: The ALICE collaboration has identified yet another possible signature of quark–gluon plasma, this time involving the directions in which particles travel after a collision.
paras.zh: ALICE 合作已经确定了夸克-胶子等离子体的另一个可能的特征，这次涉及碰撞后粒子运动的方向。

paras.en: In preliminary findings, researchers observed that particles containing three quarks (baryons) showed a stronger preference for certain directions than particles composed of two quarks (mesons) during oxygen–oxygen collisions.
paras.zh: 在初步发现中，研究人员观察到，在氧-氧碰撞过程中，包含三个夸克（重子）的粒子比包含两个夸克（介子）的粒子对某些方向表现出更强的偏好。

paras.en: This behavior is known as anisotropic flow. Rather than spreading evenly in every direction, particles emerge in patterns influenced by the conditions inside the material created during the collision.
paras.zh: 这种行为称为各向异性流。粒子不是均匀地向各个方向扩散，而是以受碰撞过程中产生的材料内部条件影响的图案出现。

paras.en: The leading explanation involves the formation of QGP. When particles with intermediate momenta emerge from this plasma, they can inherit collective motion from the quarks that make them up.
paras.zh: 最主要的解释涉及 QGP 的形成。当具有中间动量的粒子从等离子体中出现时，它们可以继承构成它们的夸克的集体运动。

paras.en: Because baryons contain three quarks while mesons contain only two, baryons can inherit more of this flow, producing the difference observed in the experiment.
paras.zh: 由于重子包含三个夸克，而介子仅包含两个夸克，因此重子可以继承更多的这种流动，从而产生实验中观察到的差异。

paras.en: This distinctive pattern provides another potential indication that the extreme matter of the early universe is being recreated in oxygen collisions.
paras.zh: 这种独特的模式提供了另一个潜在的迹象，表明早期宇宙的极端物质正在氧碰撞中重现。

paras.en: A New Window Into the Universe's First Moments
paras.zh: 进入宇宙最初时刻的新窗口

paras.en: Scientists are continuing to analyze data from collisions involving lighter atomic nuclei, searching for additional evidence of how quark–gluon plasma forms and behaves.
paras.zh: 科学家们正在继续分析涉及较轻原子核的碰撞数据，寻找夸克-胶子等离子体如何形成和行为的更多证据。

paras.en: The findings are reshaping the understanding of the conditions needed to produce one of the most extreme states of matter known to physics. What once appeared to require collisions between massive nuclei can now be investigated through much smaller systems, giving researchers new opportunities to explore the behavior of matter under extraordinary conditions.
paras.zh: 这些发现正在重塑对产生物理学已知的最极端物质状态之一所需条件的理解。曾经看似需要大质量原子核之间碰撞的东西现在可以通过更小的系统进行研究，这为研究人员提供了探索特殊条件下物质行为的新机会。

paras.en: Meanwhile, CERN is upgrading the Large Hadron Collider into the more powerful High-Luminosity LHC. The enhanced accelerator will allow scientists to collect substantially more collision data and investigate the properties of quark–gluon plasma in greater detail.
paras.zh: 与此同时，欧洲核子研究中心正在将大型强子对撞机升级为更强大的高亮度大型强子对撞机。增强型加速器将使科学家能够收集更多的碰撞数据，并更详细地研究夸克-胶子等离子体的特性。

paras.en: With each new discovery, researchers are gaining a clearer picture of the remarkable state of matter that dominated the universe during its first fleeting moments after the Big Bang.
paras.zh: 随着每一项新发现，研究人员都可以更清楚地了解宇宙大爆炸后最初转瞬即逝的瞬间主宰宇宙的物质的非凡状态。

paras.en: Materials provided by CERN. Original written by Rory Harris. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
paras.zh: 材料由欧洲核子研究中心提供。原创作者：罗里·哈里斯。注意：内容可能会根据样式和长度进行编辑。

articles.title: Scientists discover new Alzheimer’s drug that repairs DNA damage and reduces brain inflammation

paras.en: Scientists discover new Alzheimerâs drug that repairs DNA damage and reduces brain inflammation
paras.zh: 科学家发现新的阿尔茨海默病药物可以修复 DNA 损伤并减少大脑炎症

paras.en: - Scientists have discovered that a drug originally developed for spinal cord injuries can tackle several key features of Alzheimerâs disease, including DNA damage and inflammation. Already tested for initial safety in humans, the experimental treatment could offer a faster path toward therapies that target the disease at its roots.
paras.zh: - 科学家发现，一种最初开发用于脊髓损伤的药物可以解决阿尔茨海默病的几个关键特征，包括 DNA 损伤和炎症。这种实验性治疗已经在人体中进行了初步安全性测试，可以为从根源上针对疾病的治疗提供更快的途径。

paras.en: Scientists at King's College London have identified a promising new strategy for fighting Alzheimer's disease that could address several of the condition's damaging effects at the same time. Their research suggests that an experimental drug originally developed for spinal cord injuries may help repair damaged DNA, reduce inflammation, and target biological changes associated with the disease.
paras.zh: 伦敦国王学院的科学家们发现了一种对抗阿尔茨海默病的有前景的新策略，可以同时解决该病的多种破坏性影响。他们的研究表明，一种最初为脊髓损伤开发的实验药物可能有助于修复受损的 DNA、减少炎症并针对与疾病相关的生物变化。

paras.en: The drug, known as KCL-286, produced encouraging results in a mouse model of Alzheimer's disease. Unlike treatments that focus primarily on the buildup of toxic proteins in the brain, this approach targets additional processes that can begin long before the disease reaches its advanced stages.
paras.zh: 这种名为 KCL-286 的药物在阿尔茨海默病小鼠模型中产生了令人鼓舞的结果。与主要针对大脑中有毒蛋白质积聚的治疗不同，这种方法针对的是在疾病达到晚期之前很久就开始的其他过程。

paras.en: One particularly promising advantage is that KCL-286 has already completed Phase 1 human safety and tolerability trials as part of its earlier development. This could significantly shorten the path toward further clinical testing, although its effectiveness against Alzheimer's in humans has not yet been established.
paras.zh: 一个特别有前景的优势是，作为其早期开发的一部分，KCL-286 已经完成了第一阶段的人体安全性和耐受性试验。尽管尚未确定其对人类阿尔茨海默氏症的有效性，但这可能会显着缩短进一步临床测试的道路。

paras.en: "KCL-286 is a first-in-class, orally bioavailable small molecule that has already successfully cleared Phase 1 human safety and tolerability trials. This will dramatically cut down the traditional multi-year timeline required for new drug development," commented Professor Jonathan Corcoran, Professor of Neuroscience at the Institute of Psychiatry, Psychology & Neuroscience at King's College London.
paras.zh: 伦敦国王学院精神病学、心理学和神经科学研究所神经科学教授 Jonathan Corcoran 评论道：“KCL-286 是一种一流的口服生物利用小分子，已成功通过一期人体安全性和耐受性试验。这将大大缩短新药开发所需的传统多年时间。”

paras.en: The drug is a small molecule that can be taken by mouth, making it potentially more convenient to administer than treatments that require injections or infusions.
paras.zh: 该药物是一种可以口服的小分子，可能比需要注射或输注的治疗更方便。

paras.en: Why Alzheimer's Disease Is So Difficult to Treat
paras.zh: 为什么阿尔茨海默病如此难以治疗

paras.en: Alzheimer's disease involves a complicated series of changes in the brain, making it particularly challenging to develop effective treatments. Two of its best-known features are the abnormal accumulation of proteins called amyloid-beta and tau.
paras.zh: 阿尔茨海默病涉及大脑中一系列复杂的变化，因此开发有效的治疗方法尤其具有挑战性。其最著名的两个特征是β-淀粉样蛋白和tau 蛋白的异常积累。

paras.en: Amyloid-beta can collect into sticky deposits between nerve cells, while abnormal tau proteins can form tangles inside them. These changes interfere with normal brain function and are associated with the progressive loss of neurons, the specialized cells responsible for transmitting information throughout the brain.
paras.zh: β 淀粉样蛋白可以在神经细胞之间聚集成粘性沉积物，而异常的 tau 蛋白可以在神经细胞内部形成缠结。这些变化会干扰正常的大脑功能，并与神经元的逐渐丧失有关，神经元是负责在整个大脑中传递信息的特殊细胞。

paras.en: Much of the effort to develop Alzheimer's treatments has focused on these two proteins. Although medications that remove amyloid-beta have demonstrated modest but measurable clinical benefits, they do not fully address the many biological processes involved in the disease.
paras.zh: 开发阿尔茨海默病治疗方法的大部分努力都集中在这两种蛋白质上。尽管去除β-淀粉样蛋白的药物已显示出适度但可测量的临床益处，但它们并没有完全解决与该疾病有关的许多生物过程。

paras.en: Researchers are increasingly investigating other changes that may contribute to Alzheimer's, including damage to DNA and inflammation in the brain. Both can appear early in the disease process, making them potentially valuable targets for treatments designed to slow its progression.
paras.zh: 研究人员正在越来越多地研究可能导致阿尔茨海默病的其他变化，包括 DNA 损伤和大脑炎症。两者都可能出现在疾病过程的早期，这使得它们成为减缓疾病进展的治疗的潜在有价值的目标。

paras.en: In the new study, KCL-286 helped repair breaks in DNA and reduce inflammation in mice with Alzheimer's-like disease. These findings suggest that targeting several harmful processes simultaneously could offer a broader approach than focusing on amyloid-beta or tau alone.
paras.zh: 在这项新研究中，KCL-286 有助于修复患有阿尔茨海默病样疾病的小鼠的 DNA 断裂并减少炎症。这些发现表明，同时针对多个有害过程可以提供比单独关注淀粉样蛋白 β 或 tau 更广泛的方法。

paras.en: "Our findings demonstrate that KCL-286 not only targets DNA damage but also reduces inflammation, two processes that occur very early in Alzheimer's disease progression. This highlights its potential as a disease-modifying therapy rather than simply addressing symptoms," said Dr. Maria Goncalves, who project-managed the drug development.
paras.zh: “我们的研究结果表明，KCL-286 不仅针对 DNA 损伤，还可以减少炎症，这两个过程发生在阿尔茨海默病进展的早期。这凸显了它作为疾病缓解疗法的潜力，而不仅仅是解决症状，”负责药物开发项目的 Maria Goncalves 博士说。

paras.en: How Vitamin A Pathways Could Help Fight Alzheimer's
paras.zh: 维生素 A 通路如何帮助对抗阿尔茨海默病

paras.en: The drug works by activating a particular protein involved in the retinoic acid pathway, a biological system associated with how the body processes and uses vitamin A.
paras.zh: 该药物通过激活视黄酸途径中涉及的特定蛋白质发挥作用，视黄酸途径是一种与人体处理和使用维生素 A 相关的生物系统。

paras.en: Vitamin A is best known for supporting healthy vision, but it also plays important roles in cellular development, gene regulation, and nervous system function. Retinoic acid, a substance derived from vitamin A, helps control the activity of genes involved in several essential biological processes.
paras.zh: 维生素 A 因支持健康视力而闻名，但它在细胞发育、基因调节和神经系统功能中也发挥着重要作用。视黄酸是一种从维生素 A 中提取的物质，有助于控制参与多种重要生物过程的基因活性。

paras.en: Earlier research found that disruptions in this pathway were associated with the formation of amyloid-beta deposits in the brains of rats. These deposits resemble a major pathological feature of Alzheimer's disease, suggesting that the pathway may be relevant to the condition.
paras.zh: 早期研究发现，该途径的破坏与大鼠大脑中β-淀粉样蛋白沉积物的形成有关。这些沉积物类似于阿尔茨海默氏病的主要病理特征，表明该途径可能与该病有关。

paras.en: KCL-286 activates a specific protein within this system, offering researchers a way to influence biological processes connected to brain health and cellular repair.
paras.zh: KCL-286 激活该系统内的特定蛋白质，为研究人员提供了一种影响与大脑健康和细胞修复相关的生物过程的方法。

paras.en: The drug had already demonstrated an ability to promote the repair of DNA double-strand breaks in earlier research involving neuropathic pain, a type of pain caused by damage or dysfunction in the nervous system.
paras.zh: 在涉及神经病理性疼痛（一种由神经系统损伤或功能障碍引起的疼痛）的早期研究中，该药物已经证明了其促进 DNA 双链断裂修复的能力。

paras.en: That discovery led scientists to investigate whether the same mechanism might also help address DNA damage associated with Alzheimer's disease.
paras.zh: 这一发现促使科学家们研究相同的机制是否也有助于解决与阿尔茨海默病相关的 DNA 损伤。

paras.en: Repairing a Dangerous Type of DNA Damage
paras.zh: 修复危险类型的 DNA 损伤

paras.en: DNA contains the genetic instructions that cells need to function properly. Although cells have natural systems for repairing damaged DNA, some forms of damage are particularly serious.
paras.zh: DNA 包含细胞正常运作所需的遗传指令。尽管细胞具有修复受损 DNA 的天然系统，但某些形式的损伤尤其严重。

paras.en: One example is a DNA double-strand break, which occurs when both strands of the DNA molecule are severed. These breaks can disrupt normal cellular activity and threaten cell survival if they are not properly repaired.
paras.zh: 一个例子是 DNA 双链断裂，当 DNA 分子的两条链都被切断时就会发生这种情况。如果没有正确修复，这些断裂会破坏正常的细胞活动并威胁细胞的生存。

paras.en: "DNA double-strand breaks are like a rope snapping completely in two, rather than just fraying at the edges. We found that KCL-286 promotes repair of these breaks, allowing us to target a key feature of Alzheimer's disease," said Professor Corcoran.
paras.zh: “DNA 双链断裂就像一根绳子完全断成两半，而不仅仅是边缘磨损。我们发现 KCL-286 可以促进这些断裂的修复，使我们能够针对阿尔茨海默病的一个关键特征，”Corcoran 教授说。

paras.en: The researchers had another reason to suspect that KCL-286 might be useful against Alzheimer's. Previous work by the same team at King's College London identified molecular pathways shared by acute spinal cord injury and Alzheimer's disease.
paras.zh: 研究人员还有另一个理由怀疑 KCL-286 可能有助于治疗阿尔茨海默病。伦敦国王学院的同一团队之前的工作确定了急性脊髓损伤和阿尔茨海默氏病共有的分子途径。

paras.en: Because the two conditions involve some overlapping biological mechanisms, the scientists believed that a drug developed to address nervous system damage after spinal cord injury might also improve certain Alzheimer's-related changes in neurons.
paras.zh: 由于这两种情况涉及一些重叠的生物机制，科学家们认为，一种用于解决脊髓损伤后神经系统损伤的药物也可能改善某些与阿尔茨海默病相关的神经元变化。

paras.en: Their new findings support that possibility, showing that KCL-286 can influence several cellular pathways involved in the disease.
paras.zh: 他们的新发现支持了这种可能性，表明 KCL-286 可以影响与该疾病有关的多种细胞途径。

paras.en: A Promising New Direction for Alzheimer's Treatment
paras.zh: 阿尔茨海默病治疗的一个有希望的新方向

paras.en: The results highlight a potentially important shift in Alzheimer's research. Rather than concentrating on one hallmark of the disease, scientists are exploring treatments that address several interconnected causes of brain damage.
paras.zh: 研究结果凸显了阿尔茨海默病研究中潜在的重要转变。科学家们并没有专注于这种疾病的一个特征，而是正在探索解决脑损伤的几个相互关联的原因的治疗方法。

paras.en: KCL-286 is particularly interesting because it targets DNA damage and inflammation, two processes that can emerge early in Alzheimer's progression. Its previous human safety testing also provides a potential advantage over entirely new drug candidates that have not yet entered clinical development.
paras.zh: KCL-286 特别有趣，因为它针对 DNA 损伤和炎症，这两个过程可能出现在阿尔茨海默病进展的早期。其之前的人体安全测试也比尚未进入临床开发的全新候选药物具有潜在优势。

paras.en: However, the Alzheimer's findings remain preclinical. Additional studies and human clinical trials will be necessary to determine whether the drug can safely slow disease progression or improve outcomes in patients.
paras.zh: 然而，阿尔茨海默病的研究结果仍处于临床前阶段。需要进行更多的研究和人体临床试验来确定该药物是否可以安全地减缓疾病进展或改善患者的预后。

paras.en: Natasha Hill, one of the first authors on the paper, said: "To develop an effective treatment for Alzheimer's disease, we need to tackle multiple aspects of the disease. KCL-286 was able to target multiple disease-relevant cellular pathways, some of which are initiated very early in the disease course."
paras.zh: 该论文的第一作者之一 Natasha Hill 表示：“为了开发治疗阿尔茨海默病的有效疗法，我们需要解决该疾病的多个方面。KCL-286 能够靶向多种与疾病相关的细胞途径，其中一些是在病程的早期就开始的。”

paras.en: Materials provided by King's College London. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
paras.zh: 材料由伦敦国王学院提供。注意：内容可能会根据样式和长度进行编辑。

articles.title: 'VisionQuest' homework guide: Everything you need to watch to understand Marvel's WandaVision follow-up
articles.author: Jeff Spry

paras.en: Marvel Studios' existential superhero series "VisionQuest" has arrived on Disney+, and we've already been treated to four intriguing episodes that delve into the complex life of Vision, Paul Bettany's intelligent android and former card-carrying member of The Avengers.
paras.zh: 漫威影业的存在主义超级英雄系列剧《VisionQuest》已登陆 Disney+，我们已经观看了四部有趣的剧集，深入探讨了保罗·贝坦尼 (Paul Bettany) 的智能机器人、前复仇者联盟成员幻视 (Vision) 的复杂生活。

paras.en: The staggered storyline leading up to this show began with 2021's "WandaVision" and the 2024 follow-up, "Agatha All Along," with Marvel Studios proclaiming "VisionQuest" to be "the final vision of the groundbreaking trilogy." So, for those trying to catch up on current events in this trilogy of MCU shows starring Vision, and to avoid any lingering confusion, let’s take a step back to fill in the gaps.
paras.zh: 这部剧交错的故事情节始于 2021 年的《旺达幻视》和 2024 年的续集《阿加莎始终》，漫威影业宣称《幻视任务》是“开创性三部曲的最终版本”。因此，对于那些试图了解由幻视主演的漫威电影三部曲中的时事的人来说，为了避免任何挥之不去的困惑，让我们退后一步来填补空白。

paras.en: And now, this isn't as simple as just "watch all the Marvel movies and shows in order," because that is a frankly ridiculous undertaking and entirely too much homework to do before watching a show. We're distilling it down to just what you need to know to understand VisionQuest.
paras.zh: 现在，这并不像“按顺序观看所有漫威电影和节目”那么简单，因为坦率地说，这是一项荒谬的任务，而且在观看节目之前要做太多的功课。我们将其提炼为您了解 VisionQuest 所需了解的内容。

paras.en: Spoiler warning: It should go without saying, but there are spoilers for previous Marvel movies and shows in this article. You have been warned!
paras.zh: 剧透警告：这是不言而喻的，但本文中有之前的漫威电影和电视剧的剧透。您已被警告！

paras.en: TLDR: Marvel shows and movies you need to watch ahead of VisionQuest
paras.zh: TLDR：在 VisionQuest 之前您需要观看的漫威节目和电影

paras.en: We'll go into some detail on all the connections below, but if you just want a list of the essential Marvel shows and movies to watch before VisionQuest, here it is.
paras.zh: 我们将在下面详细介绍所有连接，但如果您只想在 VisionQuest 之前观看必要的漫威节目和电影的列表，这里就是。

paras.en: Note that this is just the essentials. There are loads of small references to other movies and shows in the MCU, but they're just nods.
paras.zh: 请注意，这只是必需品。有大量对漫威电影宇宙中其他电影和节目的小参考，但它们只是点头。

paras.en: - Doctor Strange and the Multiverse of Madness*
paras.zh: - 奇异博士与疯狂多元宇宙*

paras.en: *This one is debatable. It continues Wanda's story from WandaVision, but it's not really essential for understanding the events of VisionQuest.
paras.zh: *这一点值得商榷。它延续了《旺达幻视》中的旺达故事，但对于理解《幻视探索》的事件来说，这并不是真正重要的。

paras.en: Both are the true vision. Neither is the true Vision
paras.zh: 两者都是真实的愿景。都不是真正的愿景

paras.en: We kick things off with 2018's "Avengers: Infinity War," where the mighty Thanos murdered Vision by plucking out his golden, forehead-mounted Mind Stone for his Infinity Gauntlet. From that moment forward, Vision was dead, and Wanda Maximoff (Elizabeth Olsen) was cast into unfathomable grief and not-so-repressed anger.
paras.zh: 我们从 2018 年的《复仇者联盟：无限战争》开始，强大的灭霸通过拔出幻视额头上的金色心灵宝石作为他的无限手套而谋杀了他。从那一刻起，幻视死了，万达·马克西莫夫（伊丽莎白·奥尔森饰）陷入了深不可测的悲伤和无法压抑的愤怒之中。

paras.en: From there, we pick up the story in the 2021 Disney+ series "WandaVision." Set weeks after "Avengers: Endgame," this show features two separate versions of Vision.
paras.zh: 我们从这里开始讲述 2021 年 Disney+ 系列《旺达幻视》中的故事。该剧以《复仇者联盟：终局之战》几周后为背景，展示了两个不同版本的幻视。

paras.en: One was a new synthezoid version, Frankensteined together from the components of the old Vision by S.W.O.R.D., nicknamed White Vision. The other Vision is a supernatural manifestation, brought to life via Wanda Maximoff’s sorcery; he is known as Hex Vision.
paras.zh: 其中之一是新的合成版本，由 S.W.O.R.D. 的旧幻视的组件组合而成，绰号为白色幻视。另一个幻象是一种超自然现象，通过旺达·马克西莫夫的巫术得以实现。他被称为 Hex Vision。

paras.en: So, which of these two Visions appears in "VisionQuest"? That's the fun (and confusing) part, because the answer is both of them. At the end of "WandaVision," Hex Vision restores the lost memories of White Vision, essentially merging two entities into one.
paras.zh: 那么，这两个幻视中的哪一个出现在《VisionQuest》中呢？这是有趣（且令人困惑）的部分，因为答案是他们两个。在“旺达幻视”的结尾，六角幻视恢复了白色幻视失去的记忆，本质上将两个实体合二为一。

paras.en: So, the Vision we see in "VisionQuest" is the physical body of White Vision, injected with thoughts and remembrances of the model that was magically resurrected by Wanda. Confused yet? Don't worry, it's going to get weirder.
paras.zh: 所以，我们在《VisionQuest》中看到的幻视是白色幻视的肉身，注入了旺达神奇复活的模型的思想和记忆。还困惑吗？别担心，事情会变得更奇怪。

paras.en: In addition to the two versions of Vision from "WandaVision," numerous other AIs exist within Vision's skull and are all represented by human avatars acting as factions of his ravaged psyche.
paras.zh: 除了“旺达幻视”中的两个版本的幻视之外，幻视的头骨中还存在许多其他人工智能，它们都以人类化身为代表，充当他被蹂躏的心灵的派系。

paras.en: Cast your mind all the way back to 2015's "Avengers: Age of Ultron," and you'll remember that Vision was conceived from a combination of the artificial brain of Ultron, the Mind Stone, and fragments of Tony Stark’s AI butler companion, J.A.R.V.I.S., who was named after the real Jarvis seen in the "Agent Carter" TV series.
paras.zh: 回想 2015 年的《复仇者联盟：奥创纪元》，你会记得幻视是由奥创的人造大脑“心灵宝石”和托尼·斯塔克的人工智能管家伙伴贾维斯的碎片组合而成，贾维斯的名字来源于电视剧《卡特特工》中真实的贾维斯。

paras.en: J.A.R.V.I.S. appears in "VisionQuest" as his own unique entity, alongside another of Tony Stark's AI helpers, E.D.I.T.H., aka the AI in the smart glasses that Stark left to Peter Parker after his death. She shows up in "Spider-Man: Far From Home," which is a great movie but not an essential viewing if you're preparing for "VisionQuest."
paras.zh: 贾维斯在《VisionQuest》中，他作为自己独特的实体出现，与托尼·斯塔克的另一个人工智能助手 E.D.I.T.H. 一起出现，E.D.I.T.H. 又名斯塔克死后留给彼得·帕克的智能眼镜中的人工智能。她出现在《蜘蛛侠：英雄远征》中，这是一部很棒的电影，但如果你正在准备《VisionQuest》，那么这部电影并不是必不可少的观看内容。

paras.en: Then let's toss in the fact that papa Ultron (James Spader) is buzzing around in Vision’s cranium, creating what’s been described as more or less an "Age of Ultron" and a "WandaVision" sequel at the same time. As it turns out, Vision did not destroy Ultron at the end of "Age of Ultron"; he copied his code and absorbed him, so now the rabid robot lives on in Vision’s brain.
paras.zh: 然后让我们考虑一下这样一个事实：奥创爸爸（詹姆斯·斯派德饰）正在幻视的头盖骨中嗡嗡作响，同时创造了或多或少的“奥创纪元”和“旺达幻视”续集。事实证明，幻视并没有在“奥创纪元”结束时摧毁奥创；而是在“奥创纪元”结束时幻视并没有摧毁奥创。他复制了他的代码并吸收了他，所以现在这个疯狂的机器人仍然存在于幻视的大脑中。

paras.en: The show’s narrative is centered around the complicated relationship between Vision and his son Tommy Maximoff (Ruaridh Mollica). Tommy was created by Wanda's Hex and should have disappeared when it collapsed, but both he and his brother Billy survived through magical shenanigans that are explained in 2024's "Agatha All Along."
paras.zh: 该剧的叙述围绕幻视和他的儿子汤米·马克西莫夫（鲁里德·莫利卡饰）之间复杂的关系展开。汤米是由旺达的妖术创造的，在它倒塌时应该已经消失了，但他和他的兄弟比利都在神奇的恶作剧中幸存下来，这在 2024 年的《阿加莎一直》中得到了解释。

paras.en: Those two Maximoff boys, Tommy and Billy, both vanished from existence at the conclusion of "WandaVision." "Agatha All Along" exposed the truth that their consciousnesses entered the ether before expiring, only to reemerge into the souls of two teenage boys who had just perished, therefore returning them to life. Are you still with us? Good, just checking.
paras.zh: 汤米和比利这两个马克西莫夫男孩在《旺达幻视》结束时都从存在中消失了。 《始终的阿加莎》揭露了他们的意识在死亡前进入以太的真相，却又重新出现在两个刚刚死去的少年的灵魂中，从而使他们复活。你还在我们身边吗？很好，只是检查一下。

paras.en: The finale of "Agatha All Along" hinted at the return of the estranged Tommy, and "VisionQuest" dives into that dangling plot point with relish!
paras.zh: 《一直以来的阿加莎》的结局暗示了疏远的汤米的回归，而《VisionQuest》则津津有味地深入探讨了这个悬而未决的情节点！

paras.en: Every show needs an antagonist, and the voices in Vision's head can't do all the work. "VisionQuest" has introduced a duo of villains for Vision to contend with. Neither of them has shown up in the MCU previously, though, so you don't need to do any research here.
paras.zh: 每个节目都需要一个对手，而幻视头脑中的声音无法完成所有工作。 《VisionQuest》引入了一对恶棍来供Vision对抗。不过，他们之前都没有在 MCU 中出现过，所以你不需要在这里做任何研究。

paras.en: With a massive bounty on his head after breaking free from S.W.O.R.D.'s control, White Vision must contend with a new villainous foe in the form of a mysterious mercenary named Paladin (Todd Stashwick).
paras.zh: 摆脱了 S.W.O.R.D. 的控制后，怀特幻视面临着巨额悬赏，他必须对抗新的邪恶敌人，他是一位名叫圣骑士（托德·斯塔什维克饰）的神秘雇佣兵。

paras.en: This enigmatic Marvel Comics character was created by Jim Shooter and Carmine Infantino and was first seen prowling the pages of "Daredevil #150" back in 1978. He's basically a gun-for-hire in the Marvel universe, often hired to fight alongside or against various heroes depending on the story. We don't know much about his motivations in the show, but we'll learn more as it goes on.
paras.zh: 这个神秘的漫威漫画角色是由吉姆·射手和卡迈恩·因凡蒂诺创造的，第一次出现是在 1978 年的《夜魔侠 #150》中。他基本上是漫威宇宙中的雇佣枪手，经常根据故事的不同被雇佣与不同的英雄并肩作战或对抗。我们不太了解他在节目中的动机，但随着节目的继续，我们会了解更多。

paras.en: "VisionQuest" also shines a spotlight on the bizarro character of Ultron's "bride," Jocasta, though the MCU version of this character diverges wildly from the comic book inspiration.
paras.zh: 《VisionQuest》还重点关注了奥创“新娘”乔卡斯塔这一奇异角色，尽管漫威宇宙版本的这个角色与漫画中的灵感大相径庭。

paras.en: It's enough to drive one to madness! Between all the father-son dynamics dancing around the eight scheduled episodes, being hunted down by mercs, and his transcendent search for meaning, Vision and his saga are hopefully headed to a peaceful end.
paras.zh: 足以让人发疯！在围绕预定的八集跳舞的所有父子动态、被雇佣兵的追捕以及他对意义的超凡探索之间，幻视和他的传奇有望走向和平的结局。

paras.en: Created by Terry Matalas ("Star Trek: Picard," "12 Monkeys") and airing two new chapters each Tuesday night on Disney+, VisionQuest is bolstered by a cast that includes Ruaridh Mollica, T'Nia Miller, Lauren Morais, Orla Brady, Diane Morgan, Polly Frame, Henry Lewis, Jonathan Sayer, Emily Hampshire, and James D’Arcy.
paras.zh: VisionQuest 由特里·马塔拉斯（《星际迷航：皮卡德》、《十二只猴子》）创作，每周二晚上在 Disney+ 上播出两个新章节，演员阵容包括 Ruaridh Mollica、T'Nia Miller、Lauren Morais、Orla Brady、Diane Morgan、Polly Frame、Henry Lewis、Jonathan Sayer、Emily Hampshire 和 James D'Arcy。

paras.en: Jeff Spry is an award-winning screenwriter and veteran freelance journalist covering TV, movies, video games, books, and comics. His work has appeared at SYFY Wire, Inverse, Collider, Bleeding Cool and elsewhere. Jeff lives in beautiful Bend, Oregon amid the ponderosa pines, classic muscle cars, a crypt of collector horror comics, and two loyal English Setters.
paras.zh: 杰夫·斯普里 (Jeff Spry) 是一位屡获殊荣的编剧和资深自由记者，报道电视、电影、视频游戏、书籍和漫画。他的作品曾出现在 SYFY Wire、Inverse、Collider、Bleeding Cool 等网站上。杰夫住在俄勒冈州美丽的本德，周围有黄松、经典肌肉车、收藏恐怖漫画的地窖和两只忠诚的英国塞特犬。

articles.title: A rainbow of ancient rocks on Mars | Space photo of the day for Nov. 2, 2026
articles.author: Chelsea Gohd

paras.en: This rainbow-hued rocky plain looks like the landscape of an alien world. And, it turns out, it is.
paras.zh: 这片彩虹色的岩石平原看起来就像是外星世界的风景。事实证明，确实如此。

paras.en: In this image, we can see an ancient, rocky hill on Mars. In the Red Planet's Southern Highlands, this alien terrain is chock-full of minerals, which we can see clearly defined in this color-enhanced view of the region.
paras.zh: 在这张图片中，我们可以看到火星上一座古老的岩石山。在红色星球的南部高地，这片陌生的地形充满了矿物质，我们可以在该地区的色彩增强视图中清楚地看到这些矿物质。

paras.en: This image was snapped by the HiRISE camera aboard NASA's Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter (MRO), which has been studying the planet's surface, atmosphere and climate since arriving in Martian orbit in March 2006.
paras.zh: 这张照片是由 NASA 火星勘测轨道飞行器 (MRO) 上的 HiRISE 相机拍摄的，该飞行器自 2006 年 3 月抵达火星轨道以来一直在研究火星表面、大气和气候。

paras.en: But this isn't exactly what the surface of the planet would look like through our eyes; the image is color-enhanced. Why would scientists take a natural-color image and turn it rainbow? Doing so enhances the slight color differences in these rocks, allowing researchers to pick out the different minerals.
paras.zh: 但这并不完全是我们眼中地球表面的样子。图像经过色彩增强。为什么科学家要把自然色图像变成彩虹色？这样做会增强这些岩石的轻微颜色差异，使研究人员能够挑选出不同的矿物。

paras.en: As pointed to above, enhancing colors in scientific images can be an incredibly useful tool for exploration.
paras.zh: 如上所述，增强科学图像中的颜色可能是一种非常有用的探索工具。

paras.en: For instance, in this image, the blue- and green-toned rocks could be full of minerals like pyroxenes and olivine, according to scientists analyzing the image. And they think that the yellow, orange and red patches may contain minerals formed by past interactions with liquid water.
paras.zh: 例如，根据分析图像的科学家的说法，在这张图像中，蓝色和绿色色调的岩石可能富含辉石和橄榄石等矿物质。他们认为黄色、橙色和红色斑块可能含有过去与液态水相互作用形成的矿物质。

paras.en: By exploring the mineral content of rocks like this, researchers can peel back the layers of history within the Martian bedrock. The discovery of certain minerals, for example, can show that water flowed on Mars long ago, pointing to potentially habitable conditions.
paras.zh: 通过探索此类岩石的矿物质含量，研究人员可以揭开火星基岩内的历史层。例如，某些矿物质的发现可以表明很久以前火星上就有水流动，这表明火星上存在潜在的宜居条件。

paras.en: So, as we can see, this striking rainbow image isn't just a beautiful landscape; it's also hiding serious clues to Mars' history.
paras.zh: 因此，正如我们所看到的，这张引人注目的彩虹图像不仅仅是一道美丽的风景；它也是一道美丽的风景线。它还隐藏着有关火星历史的重要线索。

paras.en: Chelsea Gohd served as a Senior Writer for Space.com from 2018 to 2022 before returning in 2026, covering everything from climate change to planetary science and human spaceflight in both articles and on-camera in videos. With a M.S. in Biology, Chelsea has written and worked for institutions including NASA JPL, the American Museum of Natural History, Scientific American, Discover Magazine Blog, Astronomy Magazine, and Live Science. When not writing, editing or filming something space-y, Gohd is writing music and performing as Foxanne, even launching a song to space in 2021 with Inspiration4. You can follow her online @chelsea.gohd and @foxanne.music
paras.zh: Chelsea Gohd 于 2018 年至 2022 年担任 Space.com 的高级作家，并于 2026 年回归，在文章和视频中报道了从气候变化到行星科学和载人航天的所有内容。拥有硕士学位在生物学领域，Chelsea 曾为 NASA JPL、美国自然历史博物馆、《科学美国人》、Discover 杂志博客、天文学杂志和 Live Science 等机构撰写文章和工作。在创作、编辑或拍摄太空作品之余，Gohd 会创作音乐并以 Foxanne 的身份进行表演，甚至于 2021 年与 Inspiration4 一起向太空推出了一首歌曲。您可以在线关注她@chelsea.gohd 和@foxanne.music

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 2, 2000: Expedition 1 Arrives at the International Space Station
articles.author: Hanneke Weitering

paras.en: On Nov. 2, 2000, the International Space Station welcomed its first long-term residents: NASA astronaut Bill Shepherd and two Russian cosmonauts, Yuri Gidzenko and Sergei Krikalev. The mission was called Expedition 1.
paras.zh: 2000 年 11 月 2 日，国际空间站迎来了第一批长期居民：美国宇航局宇航员比尔·谢泼德和两名俄罗斯宇航员尤里·吉岑科和谢尔盖·克里卡列夫。这次任务被称为“远征 1”。

paras.en: Before this expedition, NASA had launched five, one-week-long Space Shuttle missions to help build the space station and bring up supplies. But this time, the crew would be staying for four and a half months, and they weren't taking the shuttle. Instead, they took a Russian Soyuz spacecraft, and this was the first Soyuz to ever dock at the space station.
paras.zh: 在这次探险之前，美国宇航局已经发射了五次为期一周的航天飞机任务，以帮助建造空间站并运送物资。但这一次，机组人员要停留四个半月，而且他们不乘坐航天飞机。相反，他们乘坐了俄罗斯联盟号飞船，这是第一艘联盟号飞船停靠在空间站。

paras.en: During their stay at the space station, they unpacked supplies and installed new equipment, including the first solar arrays. They left on the space shuttle Discovery, which brought up the Expedition 2 crew that would take their place.
paras.zh: 在空间站停留期间，他们打开了物资包装并安装了新设备，包括第一个太阳能电池阵列。他们乘坐发现号航天飞机离开，该航天飞机搭载了将接替他们的探险二号机组人员。

paras.en: As of today, there has been a continuous astronaut presence in space aboard the International Space Station for 26 years. For all of these years, not a day has gone by without someone living in space, orbiting our planet from aboard the space station.
paras.zh: 截至今天，国际空间站上的宇航员已经连续存在于太空中 26 年了。这些年来，没有一天没有人生活在太空中，从空间站绕地球运行。

paras.en: While the ISS was not the first space station, it has been the longest-running space statin by far. This first crew were pioneers, showing how humans could actually live and work aboard this station. This exploratory mission proved that the station could successfully support astronaut crews.
paras.zh: 虽然国际空间站不是第一个空间站，但它是迄今为止运行时间最长的太空他汀类药物。第一批船员是先驱者，展示了人类如何在这个空间站上实际生活和工作。这次探索性任务证明该空间站能够成功地支持宇航员。

paras.en: Since this mission 26 years ago, there have been literally hundreds of astronauts from around the world who have flown to and lived aboard the ISS. While NASA has stated that the station might be decommissioned in the coming years, these accomplishments will remain forever in spaceflight history.
paras.zh: 自 26 年前执行这项任务以来，已有数百名来自世界各地的宇航员飞往国际空间站并在其中居住。虽然美国宇航局表示该空间站可能会在未来几年退役，但这些成就将永远留在航天历史上。

paras.en: Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube.
paras.zh: 想要更多太空历史吗？查看我们完整的“太空中的这一天”故事存档，并在 YouTube 上观看“太空中的这一天”视频。

paras.en: Hanneke Weitering is a multimedia journalist in the Pacific Northwest reporting on the future of aviation at FutureFlight.aero and Aviation International News and was previously the Editor for Spaceflight and Astronomy news here at Space.com. As an editor with over 10 years of experience in science journalism she has previously written for Scholastic Classroom Magazines, MedPage Today and The Joint Institute for Computational Sciences at Oak Ridge National Laboratory. After studying physics at the University of Tennessee in her hometown of Knoxville, she earned her graduate degree in Science, Health and Environmental Reporting (SHERP) from New York University. Hanneke joined the Space.com team in 2016 as a staff writer and producer, covering topics including spaceflight and astronomy. She currently lives in Seattle, home of the Space Needle, with her cat and two snakes. In her spare time, Hanneke enjoys exploring the Rocky Mountains, basking in nature and looking for dark skies to gaze at the cosmos.
paras.zh: Hanneke Weitering 是西北太平洋地区的一名多媒体记者，在 FutureFlight.aero 和 Aviation International News 报道航空业的未来，此前曾担任 Space.com 的航天和天文学新闻编辑。作为一名拥有 10 多年科学新闻经验的编辑，她曾为学术课堂杂志、MedPage Today 和橡树岭国家实验室计算科学研究所撰写文章。在家乡诺克斯维尔的田纳西大学学习物理学后，她在纽约大学获得了科学、健康和环境报告 (SHERP) 研究生学位。 Hanneke 于 2016 年加入 Space.com 团队，担任专职撰稿人和制作人，涵盖航天和天文学等主题。她目前与她的猫和两条蛇住在太空针塔所在地西雅图。在业余时间，汉内克喜欢探索落基山脉，沐浴在大自然中，寻找黑暗的天空凝视宇宙。

articles.title: TechnoMile Recognized as a 2026 Inc. Power Partner Award Winner
articles.author: TechnoMile

paras.en: TechnoMile, the leading AI solution that unifies growth, contracts, compliance, and security workflows, has been named a 2026 Inc. Power Partner Awards winner, recognizing the company among the leading B2B partners supporting entrepreneurs and businesses across the country.
paras.zh: TechnoMile 是统一增长、合同、合规性和安全工作流程的领先 AI 解决方案，被评为 2026 年 Inc. Power 合作伙伴奖得主，认可该公司是支持全国企业家和企业的领先 B2B 合作伙伴之一。

paras.en: The annual Inc. Power Partner Awards honor B2B companies that have demonstrated a track record of helping entrepreneurs and businesses navigate the challenges of building and growing a company. From hiring and compliance to technology, infrastructure, fundraising, marketing, and more, these partners provide expertise and services that enable businesses to operate, scale, and pursue their ambitions.
paras.zh: 一年一度的 Inc. Power 合作伙伴奖旨在表彰那些在帮助企业家和企业应对创建和发展公司的挑战方面取得良好记录的 B2B 公司。从招聘和合规到技术、基础设施、筹款、营销等，这些合作伙伴提供专业知识和服务，使企业能够运营、扩大规模并实现其抱负。

paras.en: “Business owners have no shortage of tools at their disposal, and B2B companies need to make clear why their products and services are worth the investment,” says Bonny Ghosh, editorial director at Inc. “The companies on this year’s Power Partners list have done just that. They don’t just have customers – they have superfans and evangelists. Across industries like marketing, financial services, and technology, they’ve proved their dedication to helping fellow business owners grow and succeed.”
paras.zh: Inc 编辑总监邦尼·戈什 (Bonny Ghosh) 表示：“企业主并不缺乏可用的工具，B2B 公司需要明确为什么他们的产品和服务值得投资。今年 Power Partners 名单上的公司已经做到了这一点。他们不仅拥有客户，还拥有超级粉丝和传播者。在营销、金融服务和技术等行业，他们已经证明了自己致力于帮助其他企业主成长和成功。”

paras.en: TechnoMile was recognized for its investment in their clients’ long-term success, solving the persistent challenges that growing government contractors face – identifying the right opportunities among thousands of federal solicitations, managing pipelines through manual processes, lacking visibility to forecast and make confident pursuit decisions, and meeting stringent compliance and security requirements once contracts are won.
paras.zh: TechnoMile 因其对客户长期成功的投资而获得认可，解决了不断增长的政府承包商面临的持续挑战——在数千个联邦招标中识别合适的机会，通过手动流程管理管道，缺乏预测和做出自信的追求决策的可见性，以及赢得合同后满足严格的合规性和安全要求。

paras.en: TechnoMile’s unified platform connects growth, contracts, and security workflows, delivering GovCon, Defense, and Public Sector organizations greater visibility, stronger compliance, lower risk, and more efficient operations. By combining purpose-built technology, trusted AI, and deep government contracting experience, TechnoMile helps organizations compete for, win, and successfully execute mission-critical government work.
paras.zh: TechnoMile的统一平台将增长、合同和安全工作流程联系起来，为政府、国防和公共部门组织提供更高的可见性、更强的合规性、更低的风险和更高效的运营。TechnoMile将专用技术、值得信赖的人工智能和深厚的政府签约经验相结合，帮助组织争夺、赢得并成功执行关键任务的政府工作。

paras.en: “TechnoMile solves a real problem for the contracting market – providing a unified way to manage the full lifecycle of federal business,” said Ashish Khot, CEO of TechnoMile. “This award is a special honor because it is largely based on the feedback and experience of our customers and shows that we are living up to our promise to be a partner for business growth, helping companies better manage the work behind winning and delivering federal business.”
paras.zh: “TechnoMile 解决了承包市场的一个真正问题——提供统一的方式来管理联邦业务的整个生命周期，”TechnoMile 首席执行官 Ashish Khot 表示。 “这个奖项是一项特殊的荣誉，因为它主要基于我们客户的反馈和经验，表明我们正在履行我们的承诺，成为业务增长的合作伙伴，帮助公司更好地管理赢得和交付联邦业务背后的工作。”

paras.en: For more information on Inc.’s Power Partner Awards or to view the complete list of honorees, visit https://www.inc.com/power-partner-awards.
paras.zh: 有关 Inc. 电力合作伙伴奖的更多信息或查看获奖者的完整列表，请访问 https://www.inc.com/power-partner-awards。

paras.en: Inc. is the leading media brand and playbook for the entrepreneurs and business leaders shaping our future. Through its journalism, Inc. aims to inform, educate, and elevate the profile of its community: the risk-takers, the innovators, and the ultra-driven go-getters who are creating the future of business. Inc. is published by Mansueto Ventures, along with fellow leading business publication Fast Company. For more information, visit www.inc.com.

articles.title: Nov. 5: Satellite Mission Management at the Edge
articles.author: SpaceNews Editor

paras.en: Satellite operations are growing more complex. For national security missions, that means faster decisionmaking, greater resilience and the ability to adapt on orbit is needed. Today’s operators must modernize mission management, integrate new technologies and deliver capabilities without compromising security, reliability or operational control.
paras.zh: 卫星操作变得越来越复杂。对于国家安全任务来说，这意味着需要更快的决策、更强的弹性和在轨道上的适应能力。当今的运营商必须在不影响安全性、可靠性或运营控制的情况下实现任务管理现代化、集成新技术并提供功能。

paras.en: Join SpaceNews and RTX on Nov. 5 for a virtual event exploring how emerging technologies and commercial capabilities are transforming satellite operations and enabling more dynamic, resilient and affordable national security space missions.
paras.zh: 11 月 5 日与 SpaceNews 和 RTX 一起参加虚拟活动，探讨新兴技术和商业能力如何改变卫星运营，并实现更具活力、更有弹性和负担得起的国家安全太空任务。

paras.en: Speakers will discuss advances in mission management, edge computing, automation and cloud-native architectures, as well as the challenges of integrating new capabilities with legacy systems. The conversation will examine how modular approaches can accelerate technology upgrades, strengthen mission assurance and improve affordability.
paras.zh: 演讲者将讨论任务管理、边缘计算、自动化和云原生架构方面的进步，以及将新功能与遗留系统集成的挑战。对话将探讨模块化方法如何加速技术升级、加强任务保证并提高可承受性。
